tools.name: advance
tools.description: Advance the debuggers' simulation clock (%advance), running every state event, action token, change-condition poll and do behavior that comes due, in due order, and report what ran and where the debuggers stand. The clock is the session's: a debugged action and machine both move.

tools.name: apply_edits
tools.description: Apply source-preserving edits to a parsed model and return the edited notation (the ApplyEdits RPC): set a value, rename with every reference, add a member, import, documentation, comment, connection, transition, satisfy or metadata, delete, move. Edits are located from the parsed spans, so comments and layout outside them are kept, and the result is re-parsed and validated before it is answered; a refused batch answers `error` and `failure` naming why, and nothing is applied. Nothing is written to disk: the edited text comes back as `content` (one document) or `documents` for the agent to write. The result is the ApplyEditsResponse as protojson writes it.

tools.name: check_behavior
tools.description: Search every schedule of an action or state machine (the CheckBehavior RPC, the REPL's %check-property/%check-diverge settings about %action/%state): a property false at a stable state, a deadlock, a failure or a feature whose final value the schedule decides is witnessed and replayed. `verdict` is holds, fails or undecided; `violations`, `divergences` and `finals` carry each witness as its replay schedule, draws and choices, and the witness file when asked for. With checkInput or checkAssume the symbolic engine answers with `claim`, the inputs it ranged over and its witnesses. Bounded by checkDepth, checkStates and checkTimeout. The result is the CheckBehaviorResponse as protojson writes it.

instructions: OpenSysML serves SysML v2 and KerML models. The workspace tools read and edit the model documents under the server's root folder and report diagnostics as the language server does; the runtime tools parse, evaluate, instantiate, execute, verify and convert models in one call; the session tools keep a REPL session whose declarations, instances and runs persist across calls. Positions in tool arguments are 1-based line and column numbers.
